title: Trapping Rain Water
statement: Each number is the height of a unit-width bar. After rain, water collects between bars. Return the total units of water trapped.

large_tests.gen_code:
import random
def gen():
    r = random.Random(19)
    return [[r.randint(0, 1000) for _ in range(100000)]]

hints.1_question: Water above a bar is limited by the shorter of the tallest bar to its left and the tallest to its right. How could you know both without scanning every time?
hints.2_nudge: Two pointers from both ends. Whichever side currently has the shorter wall is the side whose water level is already decided.
hints.3_big_hint: Keep left_max and right_max. If height[l] < height[r]: left_max = max(left_max, height[l]); water += left_max - height[l]; l += 1. Else do the mirror image on r.

known_bugs.name: only considers the tallest bar on the left
known_bugs.code:
def trap(height):
    water = 0
    lm = 0
    for h in height:
        lm = max(lm, h)
        water += lm - h
    return water
known_bugs.followup: On a staircase going down, is there any wall on the right to hold water in? What does your code assume?

known_bugs.name: updates the running max after adding to water
known_bugs.followup: What is left_max when you first look at a bar taller than everything before it, and what does `left_max - height` become?

known_bugs.name: rescans for max on both sides of every bar (O(n^2))
known_bugs.followup: How many elements does max() look at for each bar? Can you carry the running maximum instead?
